name: CGCI
full_name: CGCI (Catheter Guidance Control and Imaging) remote magnetic navigation system
versions: single system: animal validation in 10 pigs (gang2011_dynamically, abstract); initial human safety and feasibility protocol at La Paz University Hospital, Madrid, 5 flutter ablations (filgueirasrama2013_remote, Table 1); later discontinued (mandhumula2025_robotic: 'now seems to have been discontinued', 'not adopted commercially')
target_anatomy: cardiac electrophysiology: right and left atrial flutter ablation (filgueirasrama2013_remote Table 1); pig left atrium mapping and RF lesions (gang2011_dynamically abstract)
devices_driven: magnetized irrigated gold-tip EP ablation catheter (MedFact) with three permanent-magnet pellets at the tip, through an Agilis ES sheath (filgueirasrama2013_remote Protocol 1, Fig. 1); 4-mm-tip ablation catheter in pigs (gang2011_dynamically abstract); catheter 7 Fr / 2.2 mm (jeong2017_feasibility Introduction)
n_dof_detail: 3 (mandhumula2025_robotic Table 1; alekseeva2025_design Table 14); field shaped by 8 coil-core electromagnets, push-pull by field gradient (filgueirasrama2013_remote Representative Results) plus a motorized linear catheter advancer
translation_detail: magnetic (field-gradient push-pull at the tip); motorized linear catheter advancement mechanism with a sterilizable wheel-drive gearbox on a motor base, joystick-controlled slack/advance (filgueirasrama2013_remote Protocol 1, Fig. 2A, 2C)
rotation_detail: tip direction by dynamically shaped field of 8 fixed electromagnets, 4 above and 4 below the patient in a semi-spherical chamber (li2020_magnetic Sec. 3.3; gang2011_dynamically abstract)
footprint_mm: N.R. (semi-spherical chamber of 8 electromagnets around the torso, li2020_magnetic Fig. 5)
haptics_leader: no: right-hand 3D controller and left-hand 3-axis joystick at a remote operation console (filgueirasrama2013_remote Fig. 2B-C)
imaging_compat: X-ray fluoroscopy, EnSite NavX electroanatomic mapping, EP recording and ICE unified at the operation console (filgueirasrama2013_remote Protocol 1); recording and fluoroscopic equipment unaffected by the fields (gang2011_dynamically abstract)
sterility: sterilizable wheel-drive gearbox, disposable sheath clip and leg mount on the advancer (filgueirasrama2013_remote Fig. 2A)
validation_detail: human: 5 atrial flutter ablations (3 left, 2 counterclockwise right), acute success 5/5, no procedure-derived complications, no recurrence at 3-11 months (filgueirasrama2013_remote Table 1); animal: 10 pigs, left-atrial mapping, linear and circumferential RF lesions, selective PV isolation in a subset (gang2011_dynamically abstract)
key_numbers: field up to 0.16 T (filgueirasrama2013_remote Protocol 1); 0.14 T and 0.7 T/m gradients (mandhumula2025_robotic text); pigs, automated mode: 96 +/- 8.4% reproducible, 1.9 +/- 0.4 mm from target, 11.6 +/- 3.5 s to target, lesion depth 78.5 +/- 12.1% of atrial wall (gang2011_dynamically abstract); five initial experimental procedures: 95.7% reproducible, 1.9 +/- 0.9 mm, 23.28 +/- 14.8 s (filgueirasrama2013_remote Representative Results)
